question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=4x(t)-8y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2x(t)-4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ of the system's matrix $A$ is $v=[2,\text{ }1]^{T}.$ The vector $w={[\frac{1}{2},0]}^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$  Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the system?

*Hint: Here, the dotted line represents the equilibrium solutions.*
question.worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =0$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $v,$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}v{e}^{\lambda t}+{c}_{2}(vt{e}^{\lambda t}+w{e}^{\lambda t}\,),
$$

where $w$ is a solution to the equation $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$

In our case, 

$$
\lambda =0,\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2t+\frac{1}{2} \\ t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that ${x}_{E}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ are equilibrium solutions of the system since ${x}_{E}^{′}(t)=0.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=\frac{1}{2}x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/bff5cf9d21f0b01571b577ebe3d98ef08525d13a70a1d7379b537f6ba5319613.png)

Now, we consider some general solutions of the form 

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2t+\frac{1}{2} \\ t\end{aligned}].
$$

For example:

- When ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=2,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=4t+3 \\ y=2t+1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/7d590ee38f7f1b6b43c9b650890f42fa31b4c15951dab8bcb003b1ac1cc45c39.png)

- When ${c}_{1}=-1$ and ${c}_{2}=-2,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-4t-3 \\ y=-2t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/b965e3e244bc49b5e0f52840550c2ae997a0e38dc40e8757f0f51905c448d7af.png)

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226345/assets/1b785127a21453e56d7d0df4f641133a44d2109008e21f8bd3057d8ac22a351f.png)
